//: web/tsconfig.json is a SOLUTION file: `"files": []` plus a reference to
tsconfig.app.json. That is the standard Vite layout and `tsc -b` handles it
correctly, following the reference and type-checking src and tests/browser.
The editor does not. VS Code opens a .tsx file, walks up to the nearest
tsconfig.json, finds a project that includes NO files, and falls back to
implicit defaults -- which have no "jsx": "react-jsx" and no DOM lib. Every
JSX tag then reports "JSX element implicitly has type 'any' because no
interface 'JSX.IntrinsicElements' exists", while `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
Pointing the TS server at the real project resolves it. Committed rather than
left to each developer, because an editor that reports errors the build does
not is how a real error gets ignored as noise.
The same empty-root-project trap caused a shipped build failure on
2026-08-06: `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` was run as a gate, checked
nothing, and exited 0. See the note in the Makefile's lint target -- always
use the project's own `npm run typecheck`.
